justification: Carrying span: “in the cold the first blow took the cone two-thirds as deep, and the count nearly doubled” — cold grid = shallower first blow, higher blow-count, exactly C. A dies on the instrument's own definition: it reports “how many blows take it to a hundred millimetres” while “The floor is 130 millimetres”, so the cone is never driven to the bottom of the bed. B dies on “a ring weight raised to a collar and let fall” — a collar fixes the drop height, so it is not “from whatever height each point seemed to need”. D is the stated relation reversed: “The gap between my February morning and my July afternoon is still wider than the gap between this school and any other school I test” makes the between-visits spread the wider one, not the between-arenas spread.

Carrying span: “Pallenmoor cored the bed in eleven places. In the top 50 millimetres the fibre came out at about 8 per cent by weight; lower down it was nearer 3” — much less fibre at the bottom than the top, D. A is contradicted by “the wax he brought up from the bottom was in better condition than the wax at the top”. B is contradicted by “the grains he sieved came out much as the original specification had them”. C inverts the finding: the sub-tine 80 mm “had not been turned since the day it was laid, and under nine years of hoofprints it had gone firm enough to lean a spade on” — firm, and reached by the hoofprints, not loose and out of reach.

Carrying span: “In the schools laid on plain sand and fibre and kept damp with a sprinkler, the morning grid and the afternoon grid sit almost on top of one another. The waxed ones move, whatever their age”, with the mechanism named in “The wax is a paraffin blend, and it is doing most of that work” — absence of wax is what leaves them steady, B. A dies on “whatever their age” plus “some of them older than this one”, which explicitly removes age as the explanation. C dies on “plain sand and fibre” — these schools have no coating at all, so no supplier's blend can be holding its state. D dies on “the morning grid and the afternoon grid” — the same two reading times are used, so the change cannot be falling outside them.

Carrying span: “Here Pallenmoor is careful, and the care is the most useful thing about him”, where the care is precisely the limiting — “I can't put a number on it; these readings won't carry one”, “The tester measures a surface; there is no horse above the cone”, “he would argue it from the veterinary literature rather than from his own figures” — so the writer takes his self-imposed limits to be the real contribution, A. B fails because §5 reports the yard's changes (tines to 80 mm, “Heaters have been costed and not ordered”) with no framing as an answer on soundness, which §4 has just declared out of the readings' reach. C inverts the roles: the riders' account (“hard and slippery for a January lesson, deep and tiring by a July afternoon”) is what the readings confirm; what they correct is the yard's blame — “The yard has blamed the machine, then the mix, then the man on the tractor”. D reverses the closing judgement “That is a good deal less than the trade's brochures offer, and it is worth more than they are”.

Carrying spans: temperature — “Below about six degrees the coating is stiff, the grains lock together, and a hoof breaks the surface. Above about twenty-five it goes slack … and the floor gets deep”; tine depth — “The leveller's tines were set to 50 millimetres. The bed is 130 … the machine had been slowly sorting the bed into a loose layer riding on a hard one”, with “Then there is the machine, though not in the way the yard had blamed it” keeping it a real second factor. Both bear on how the floor rides, so C. A misnames the mechanism: the locking is stiffened paraffin coating, not ice — the cold reading is “three degrees”, above freezing, and the sprinkler-damp schools, the wettest ones, are the schools that do not move. B is an extrapolation the text refuses: heaters were “costed and not ordered”, so no warmed school was ever read, and “I can't put a number on it; these readings won't carry one” blocks the quantitative prediction, which the “about twenty-five” slack threshold also breaks. D reverses the direct quotation “The temperature is doing more in that room than the tractor is.”

The gap joins two parallel instances of one phenomenon: the start is unanimous with no signal (“there is no conductor to watch, and yet two hundred people find the same half-second”) and so is the finish (“the ending is unanimous … and again there has been no signal”). “Equally” marks that likewise relation, C. A “Hence” asserts a causal link the text does not make — the unanimous ending is not produced by the unanimous start, it is a second case of the same puzzle. B “Rather” demands a correction of what precedes, but “again there has been no signal” reinforces rather than corrects. D “Elsewhere” shifts location, while both halves describe the same hall and the same performance.

The needed sense is participation: the risk is that the room may not join in, leaving you “alone with an opinion nobody asked for”, and the next sentence confirms it — “that is why the second pair of hands matters more than the first”, i.e. somebody joining. A. B “cut in” means to interrupt or interject; the room failing to interrupt is not the risk described, which is being left unaccompanied. C “fall in” means to form up in line, not to add one's applause to another's. D “break in” means to interrupt or to enter by force; neither sense yields the room adding its hands to yours.

The gap names an ongoing wordless process, not its result: “the coming-down is a ___ about how long is decent, conducted at speed and without words” — “conducted” collocates with negotiation, and the descent is the working-out itself, B. A “transaction” is an exchange of goods or money and takes no “about how long is decent” complement. C “bargain” names the deal struck, an outcome one strikes rather than conducts, whereas the sentence equates the gap with “the coming-down”, a process in progress. D “settlement” likewise names the resolution reached, not the reaching, and cannot be “conducted at speed”.

“Although” requires the gap to state something that would argue for long applause, against which “it is not permitted to run long” stands as concession; warmth conceded against duration gives “wholehearted”, D, and the following “Four or five seconds, then a ragged tail” supplies the short duration being conceded. C “brief” collapses the concession into a restatement — “although brief, not permitted to run long” is no contrast at all. A “rehearsed” contradicts the piece's premise that nothing is arranged (“No one has agreed to anything”, “not one of the people in it could explain how”) and sets up no concession about length. B “outspoken” describes a person's readiness to voice opinions, not what a hall gives a child, and again bears on manner rather than duration.

The clause turns on applause that is solicited rather than spontaneous — “A room asked for a big hand for a stranger” — and the room complies while “everybody present can hear that it is not the same sound the recorder player got”; compliance without warmth is “dutifully”, B. A “narrowly” means barely or in a restricted respect and does not describe the manner of giving applause. C “instinctively” contradicts “asked for”, the very feature that makes this the case where “the mechanism … slips”; the instinctive case is the recorder player's. D “eagerly” would make the sound as good as or better than the recorder player's, destroying the stated audible shortfall.

Carrying span: Ashvenor's own quotation after the accelerometer week — “Between stations the shocks were tiny. ‘It's the stop at the far end that does it,' she says” — locating the damage at arrival at the far end, A. B is contradicted by “Nothing shows on the ward; the colour comes with the spinning”. C is contradicted by “Blood gases have never gone by tube; a porter walks those down” — they do not go by tube at all. D misattributes the improvement: “The loop runs at the speed it always has. Two bins are lined with foam, and rejects are down by about half” — the fall follows the foam lining, with speed expressly unchanged.

The implication rests on two spans that describe one stretch of ground: the claim covers “the bank, the ditch and the timber from the stone gap down to the lane”, and the survey ran “along the bank, from the ash to the culvert”, where “An ash grew in the stone gap; a culvert ran under the lane” — identical endpoints, so the claimed ground is the pegged ground, D. C reverses the chronology: the pegging was “The previous October”, before the claim of “November 1845” at which the letters begin. A is contradicted by “The neighbour's attorney enclosed a tracing of the railway company's deposited plan”. B fails because the bank was tended by both — “cut from above by one and cleaned from below by the other” — and the agreed last laying, 1839, is given as common ground rather than as grievance; nothing ties neglect to the outbreak, whereas the survey date does.

Bärande sats: “Ändå ska den bäras. Från och med nästa spelår bör texten gå på varje föreställning på stora scenen, inte på fyra utvalda”, kombinerad med medgivandet om spelet: “Textremsan låser repliken … den som vet att remsan går spelar inte som förut. Så lyder ensemblens invändning, och jag skriver under på den” — precis A:s “även om spelet binds hårdare vid manus”. B motsägs ordagrant av “Ett svepskäl är det inte. Kostnaden är verklig och ska räknas med”. C motsägs två gånger: “Fler särskilda kvällar begär jag inte” och “Att ensemblen vänjer sig vid remsan kan jag inte lova”. D motsägs av att skribenten uttryckligen avstår från förslag för lilla scenen: “Om lilla scenen kan bära samma sak vet jag inte … och något förslag för den scenen har jag inte.”

Bärande sats: “I länsteaterns höstprogram har de textade föreställningarna en egen rad, inklämd mellan syntolkning och skolföreställningar” — D. A och B tillskriver raden det som gäller slingsymbolen: “Slingans symbol finns längst ned på varje uppslag i programbladet” — symbolen står på varje uppslag och märker inte raden för textade föreställningar. C stupar på placeringen: den tekniskt ansvariga anges på annat ställe — “Längre bak i programbladet står Ingegerd Hörnfeldt under rubriken Text och teknik” — inte på raden.

Bärande sats: “Skaren som bar en karl gick sönder under hoven”, med förklaringen “En hov samlar hela djurets tyngd på en yta stor som en tallrik” — hovarna sjönk igenom där folk bar, A. B motsägs av “och mot det hjälper varken broddar eller lättare lass”. C motsägs av “Lassen gick på kälke i stället, och kälken drogs för hand” — kälkarna drogs alltså av människor, inte av hästar. D saknar täckning: texten säger “Hästen fick stå i stallet” och nämner ingen annan syssla för hästarna under skarveckorna.

Bärande satser: “Veckorna kom när de kom” och “Man såg på himlen och bestämde sig kvällen innan”, förstärkt av “Somliga år blev det fyra morgnar på hela vintern, och ett par vintrar uteblev skaren” — dagarna kunde inte bestämmas i förväg, B. A motsägs av “Var gård körde för sig, och sällan väntade någon in grannen”. C flyttar en nutidsbild till arbetet: “Barnen provar den med hälen som vi gjorde, utan att det ska bli någon färd” — barnen provar i dag och just utan färd, de gick inte före lassen. D motsägs av “avstånden krymper till raka linjer” och “en väg som inte finns resten av året”.

The waxed ones move, whatever their age', with the mechanism supplied by 'The wax is a paraffin blend, and it is doing most of that work.' The absence of wax is the named differentiator. Heaters have been costed and not ordered' - while the soundness question stands unanswered on 'The tester measures a surface; there is no horse above the cone.' Carrier: two spans jointly - 'Below about six degrees the coating is stiff, the grains lock together, and a hoof breaks the surface. Above about twenty-five it goes slack... and the floor gets deep' and 'The leveller's tines were set to 50 millimetres. The bed is 130... the machine had been slowly sorting the bed into a loose layer riding on a hard one', with the remedy 'The tines have been dropped to 80 millimetres'. Temperature and tine depth are the two stated determinants of how the floor rides. A killed: the stated mechanism is the wax, not ice - 'Below about six degrees the coating is stiff, the grains lock together' - and the cold grid was read 'with the school at three degrees', above freezing, while the watered sprinkler schools do not move at all. B killed: the thresholds forbid it - a heated February school sits between 'about six' and 'about twenty-five' whereas the July afternoon is the slack end - and 'Heaters have been costed and not ordered', so no such school exists in the text. Carrier: the gap joins two parallel unanimities - 'two hundred people find the same half-second' and '___, the ending is unanimous: five seconds later the sound stops, and again there has been no signal.' The word 'again' marks the addition of a like case, which 'Equally' supplies. A killed: 'Hence' asserts consequence, but the unanimous ending is not caused by the unanimous start; it is presented as a second instance of the same puzzle. B killed: 'Rather' corrects or replaces a prior claim, and nothing in 'No one has agreed to anything, there is no conductor to watch' is being retracted. Carrier: 'The risk of putting your hands together in a quiet room is that the room may not ___ in, and for the length of one clap you are alone with an opinion nobody asked for', confirmed by 'That is why the second pair of hands matters more than the first' - the risk is the room not joining in. B killed: 'cut in' means to interrupt something already running; the risk here is that nobody follows. C killed: the agreement sense of 'fall in' requires 'fall in with' plus an object, which the bare '___ in' slot cannot carry; bare 'fall in' means to form up in line. D killed: 'break in' likewise means to intrude or interrupt, the opposite of the room failing to come with you.

Carrier: 'the coming-down is a ___ about how long is decent, conducted at speed and without words' - 'conducted' plus 'about how long is decent' requires an ongoing wordless process of settling a question, matching 'A hall organises itself in about a fifth of a second'. A killed: a 'transaction' is an exchange of goods or money and is not 'about' a question of decency. C killed: a 'bargain' is the struck outcome ('strike a bargain'), not a thing 'conducted', while the sentence describes the coming-down in progress. D killed: a 'settlement' is likewise the resolution arrived at, so it cannot be what is 'conducted at speed'.

Carrier: the concessive frame 'Although what a hall gives an eight-year-old is ___, it is not permitted to run long' needs a quality pulling against brevity; 'wholehearted' supplies it, and the cap follows - 'Four or five seconds, then a ragged tail'. A killed: 'rehearsed' contradicts 'No one has agreed to anything, there is no conductor to watch' and yields no contrast with running long. B killed: 'outspoken' describes a person's speech, not applause given to a child, and again sets up no concession. C killed: 'brief' makes the Although-clause agree with its main clause ('not permitted to run long'), collapsing the concession.

Carrier: 'A room asked for a big hand for a stranger will give one ___, and everybody present can hear that it is not the same sound the recorder player got' - applause produced on request and audibly hollow is given dutifully. A killed: 'narrowly' means by a small margin or in a restricted sense and does not describe manner of clapping. C killed: 'instinctively' contradicts the trigger - the room was 'asked' - and the spontaneous case in this text is the recorder player's, from which this one is expressly distinguished. D killed: 'eagerly' would make the sound indistinguishable from the real thing, which the clause denies: 'it is not the same sound'.

Carrier: 'Between stations the shocks were tiny. "It's the stop at the far end that does it," she says.' - the cells burst on arrival, not in transit. Two bins are lined with foam, and rejects are down by about half' - the fall follows the foam lining, not any slowing.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: soft type-split. The stem “What is said about Pallenmoor’s work in the school?” mildly selects the two method statements (A and B) over the two findings (C and D), but the narrowing is weak because findings are legitimately things said about his work.

Considered and rejected as decisive: “from whatever height each point seemed to need” describes an uncontrolled drop height and reads as a deliberate methodological-flaw distractor, which favours “He drove the cone through to the bottom of the bed at each point.” only marginally.
No modalised option in the set; no absolutizer-only-in-distractors pattern.
justification: A and B are the two method statements, and B's uncontrolled drop height tips the pair toward A. Genuinely near coin-flip once the type-split is applied, and the split itself is soft. Top option about 30 percent. No channel reaches the flag bar on its own.

findings: MIRRORED_TWIN: “The wax had worn off the grains in the lower part of the bed.” and “There was much less fibre in the bottom of the bed than in the top.” are structurally identical claims - the bottom of the bed is depleted of an additive - differing only in the noun; twinned options cancel for a passage-blind reader.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE: “Below the tines the bed had stayed loose, out of reach of the hoofprints above it.” inverts the expected physics, since traffic compaction reaches below harrow depth and the layer under the tines sets hard rather than staying loose; any reader with surface or soil intuition discards it.
The residual option carries the concrete checkable detail “finer grains than the specification called for”, which is typical key phrasing.
justification: The twin-cancel on A and D plus the inverted-physics elimination of C leaves B as the residual. The chain is heuristic, not certain: about 45 to 50 percent on B. Sub-kill but a real two-step passage-blind route.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: contradictory pair on one variable. “Having no wax on their sand is what leaves them riding much the same all day.” asserts these schools have no wax; “Their coating is a blend from another supplier, and it holds its state as the day warms.” asserts they have a coating. Same variable, incompatible values. Scored as a channel per binding calibration.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: B and C also share the explanandum the stem points at, how these schools behave through the day, while “They went down more recently, so their sand has not had nine years of hooves on it.” and “They are read at a different hour, so the change falls between his two grids.” explain something else, so the field collapses to the contradictory pair.
CROSS_QUESTION: the remove-the-temperature-sensitive-variable thesis is echoed in q:5 by “A school that is kept warm will ride in February much as it rides in July.”; picking one raises the other.
justification: Per binding calibration a contradictory pair on one variable is a channel; here it is a one-versus-one contradiction inside a four-set with the other two options on unrelated variables, which narrows to roughly fifty-fifty on B and C. B is favoured because “kept damp with a sprinkler” and a wax coating are alternative surface regimes, so a coating claim sits awkwardly with the stem. Top option about 50 percent: flag, not kill.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (register): exactly one option is a meta or epistemic-humility stance, “She takes the limits he sets on his own figures to be his real contribution.”, which is the archetypal key shape for an ELF writer's-position item; the other three are first-order positions.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (register): “She rates the trade’s brochures the fuller answer to the question the yard is asking.” is discardable on register alone, since no serious writer prefers commercial brochures to measurements.
Whole-text item: this is one of two whole-text claims in the unit.
justification: Genre sense alone, with no equestrian knowledge, gets a Swedish 18-year-old to A: discard D on register, then prefer the humility-praising meta stance over the two first-order stances. “She reads what the yard has since done as an answer to the soundness question.” and “She treats the riders’ account as the thing the readings were brought in to correct.” stay live enough to hold A to about 55 percent, so this is a flag rather than a kill, and it is the closest non-kill in the ELF long unit.

findings: NOT SCORED per brief: “In the cold the grains are probably freezing to one another in a school with no heating.” and “The tractor’s work may matter more to the school than the temperature does.” are hedged against two flat options. findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE (expert-only, non-decisive): “A spoilt sample can be spotted by its colour before it leaves the ward.” is false to anyone with laboratory knowledge, since haemolysis is judged on spun serum at the laboratory and not by eye on a whole-blood tube, but a Swedish 18-year-old would need to know how haemolysis is detected, which is not school knowledge, so the elimination is not student-available.
No modalised option, no absolutizer pattern, no twin pair; single-item unit, so no cross-question surface.
justification: “The harm is done at the moment a carrier reaches the far end.” is favoured as the counterintuitive mechanism claim such a piece is built around and as the only option locating harm at a moment; “The number of rejected samples fell once the loop was slowed down.” reads as an intervention-outcome distractor and “Samples for blood gases go by tube because they cannot be left waiting.” as a true-sounding aside. About 45 percent on A, reached by genre reasoning rather than by any structural channel. No student-available leak: pass.

findings: ENTAILMENT / PAIR_STRUCTURE (strong form, within one question): the proposition that a railway surveyor pegged out ground on the bank while attorneys were exchanging letters survives across three of the four options. “Ruddiforth’s neighbour answered the claim without bringing the railway company’s plan into the letters.” names the plan and the letters; “The surveyor came to the bank after the attorneys had begun to write.” names the surveyor and the attorneys; “The ground Ruddiforth was claiming was the same ground the surveyor had pegged out.” names the pegged-out ground. Neither stem supplies any of it; the option set alone hands a passage-blind reader the whole situation.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: “The quarrel began because the thorn on the bank had been left untended.” is the only option outside that shared world, and the stem “What is implied about the quarrel between the neighbouring farms?” rarely keys to a plain stated cause, so B is discardable without the passage. That elimination is student-available and needs no domain knowledge.
justification: Eliminating B leaves a three-way field. D is favoured as the option that unifies the shared elements into a motive, which is the shape an implied-stem usually rewards. But A and C jointly encode the opposite twist, that the quarrel predates and is independent of the railway, and that reading is coherent enough to hold D to about 45 percent. Flag on the shared-presupposition leak, not a kill.

findings: 3+1 exclusivity cluster (INERT per binding calibration): “Allt på stora scenen bör textas, även om spelet binds hårdare vid manus.”, “Antalet textade kvällar bör utökas i den takt som ensemblen vänjer sig vid remsan.” and “En skärm bör hänga ovanför lilla scenen också, trots att publiken där sitter nära skådespelarna.” are three prescriptions on a scope variable, against the motive diagnosis “Ensemblens invändning mot textremsan är ett svepskäl som döljer ett annat motstånd.”; treated as inert, not scored.

No modalised option: the constructions “även om”, “trots att” and “i den takt som” are concessive, not modal. “Allt” is the only absolutizer, so the every-distractor-absolutized pattern does not fire.
Whole-text item: the stem “Vilken inställning har skribenten till textning på länsteatern?” is the unit's one whole-text stance claim.
justification: Near-flat field: A about 30 percent, C about 25 percent, D about 23 percent, B about 22 percent. The concessive framing in A and D is mildly key-shaped and C is the compromise stance, but nothing separates them without the text. A picked on the concessive-plus-scope reading only. No scoreable channel: pass.

findings: No scoreable channel: “Den är märkt med slingans symbol.”, “Den upprepas längst ned på varje uppslag.”, “Den anger vem som sköter tekniken.” and “Den ligger mellan syntolkningen och skolföreställningarna.” are four mutually exclusive properties of one line in a programme, matched for length and register.

Considered and rejected: A conflates the hearing loop with captioning and C names a technician the audience does not need, but neither elimination is safe, since venues do group access services under one mark and small theatres do credit captioning partners, so the narrowing is not real.
justification: D is the only positional claim and position is the shape a text describing a season programme usually states, but that is a weak preference: D about 33 percent, B about 27 percent, A about 20 percent, C about 20 percent. Effectively a clean detail item. Pass.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE (strong form): the premise of a crust that carries people but not hooves, during a bounded few weeks, survives across three of four options. “Hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick.” states the hoof half, “Hovarna klarade sig med broddar.” presupposes a hoof traction problem, and “Hästarna användes till annat under de veckorna.” supplies the bounded season. Neither stem supplies any of it, so the situation is recoverable from the option set alone.

CROSS_QUESTION / symmetric vouching with q:2, whose option “Barnen fick gå först och prova skaren med hälen.” names “skaren” outright and presupposes that human weight is the safe probe, confirming the half of the variable that A asserts.
justification: Once the crust premise is recovered, “Hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick.” is the only option that states the text's evident physical point, and its competitors do not cohere with the q:2 option set the way A does. About 45 percent on A. The leak is real and bidirectional, but it does not by itself put any option at 60 percent, so flag.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE / CROSS_QUESTION: the q:1 option set supplies the crust-and-bounded-season frame, and that frame kills “Man tog samma vägar som resten av året.” outright, since the point of hauling on a crust is that it opens ground impassable the rest of the year; the option is dead on arrival for a reader who has read the q:1 options.

CROSS_QUESTION: the same frame raises “Barnen fick gå först och prova skaren med hälen.” and “Det gick inte att bestämma dagarna i förväg.”, since a crust forms only after a thaw-freeze cycle, so the leak both removes and promotes options.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE: the stem “Vad framgår av texten om hur arbetet lades upp?” asks about “hur arbetet lades upp”, and C is a procedure inside the work rather than an organising principle, which pulls against the option the leak promotes.
justification: Estimates: B about 35 percent, C about 27 percent, A about 25 percent, D about 13 percent. The cross-question elimination of “Man tog samma vägar som resten av året.” is a genuine passage-blind gain, from a 25 percent baseline to about 35 percent on the top option, so flag; but the two most-vouched answers are not the stem-fit favourites, which keeps the top option well under the kill line.

findings: A (key): "Från och med nästa spelår bör texten gå på varje föreställning på stora scenen, inte på fyra utvalda." — the proposal itself; the concession clause matches 'Textremsan låser repliken' plus 'Ändå ska den bäras.'
B: "Ett svepskäl är det inte." — the writer explicitly denies the ensemble's objection is a pretext, and adds 'Kostnaden är verklig och ska räknas med.'
C: "Fler särskilda kvällar begär jag inte." — she rejects more special evenings outright, and 'Att ensemblen vänjer sig vid remsan kan jag inte lova' denies the pacing condition C builds in.
D: "Om lilla scenen kan bära samma sak vet jag inte." — she withholds judgement on the small stage: 'något förslag för den scenen har jag inte'.
justification: The writer's position is stated in one sentence (every performance on the big stage from next season) and she concedes the acting cost rather than denying it, which is exactly A's 'även om spelet binds hårdare vid manus'. Each distractor inverts an explicit denial: B inverts 'Ett svepskäl är det inte', C inverts her refusal of more special evenings, D inverts her refusal to propose anything for the small stage.

findings: D (key): "I länsteaterns höstprogram har de textade föreställningarna en egen rad, inklämd mellan syntolkning och skolföreställningar." — the row's position between audio description and school performances is stated in the opening sentence.
A: "Slingans symbol finns längst ned på varje uppslag i programbladet och har gjort det i alla år." — the loop symbol sits at the foot of every spread, not on the captioned-performance row.
B: "Slingans symbol finns längst ned på varje uppslag i programbladet" — what recurs at the foot of every spread is the loop symbol; the row itself appears once, holding four evenings.
C: "Längre bak i programbladet står Ingegerd Hörnfeldt under rubriken Text och teknik." — the technician is named further back under her own heading, not on the row.
justification: D restates the first sentence. A, B and C each attach to the row a property the passage assigns to something else in the same programme (the loop symbol twice, the Text och teknik entry once), which is a clean single-span kill in every case.

findings: A (key): "Skaren som bar en karl gick sönder under hoven" — the crust that carried a man broke under the hoof - exactly A; the reason is given as 'En hov samlar hela djurets tyngd på en yta stor som en tallrik'.
B: "mot det hjälper varken broddar eller lättare lass" — studs explicitly did not help.
C: "Lassen gick på kälke i stället, och kälken drogs för hand." — the sledge was pulled by hand, not by the horses.
D: "Hästen fick stå i stallet." — the horse stayed in the stable; no other employment for it is mentioned anywhere in the passage.
justification: A is a near-verbatim restatement with a stated mechanism (a hoof concentrates the animal's whole weight on a plate-sized area). B and C are contradicted word for word; D adds a fact the passage never supplies.

findings: B (key): "Veckorna kom när de kom." — reinforced by 'Man såg på himlen och bestämde sig kvällen innan' and by the year-to-year spread (three weeks one year, four mornings another, some winters none) - the days could not be fixed ahead.
A: "Var gård körde för sig, och sällan väntade någon in grannen." — each farm drove for itself, the opposite of households taking turns and sharing the trips.
C: "Barnen provar den med hälen som vi gjorde, utan att det ska bli någon färd." — the only children in the text are present-day ones testing the crust for fun; no loading role is mentioned.
D: "Ett lass som inte är hemma vid tio blir liggande till nästa natt." — work stopped when the crust gave way at ten; a load not home by then was abandoned until the next night.
justification: B is the intended reading and the three others are each contradicted by an explicit span. Minor nuance noted, not disqualifying: 'bestämde sig kvällen innan' is technically a decision made in advance, but an evening-before call driven by reading the sky is the passage's own illustration that the days could not be planned, and no rival option survives, so B is not in competition with anything.

findings: C (key): "in the cold the first blow took the cone two-thirds as deep, and the count nearly doubled" — two-thirds as deep = shallower first blow; count nearly doubled = higher count. Both match C.

A: "how many blows take it to a hundred millimetres" — the count stops at 100 mm while 'The floor is 130 millimetres of washed silica sand', so the cone is not driven to the bottom; the coring in eleven places is a separate operation.
B: "a steel cone on a rod, under a ring weight raised to a collar and let fall" — the collar fixes the drop height, which is what makes the blow count comparable; nothing is judged by eye per point.
D: "The gap between my February morning and my July afternoon is still wider than the gap between this school and any other school I test." — D reverses the comparison Pallenmoor actually makes.
justification: Arithmetic and comparison both reconcile. 100 mm < 130 mm kills A outright. The two figures move in the same direction for hardness: a first blow at two-thirds depth and a blow count near double are consistent with a stiffer bed - not a linear identity (linear scaling would predict about 1,5x, and penetration resistance rising with depth accounts for the rest), which is why the writer has him refuse a number: 'I can’t put a number on it; these readings won’t carry one'. D is the within-arena-versus-between-arena comparison inverted.

findings: D (key): "In the top 50 millimetres the fibre came out at about 8 per cent by weight; lower down it was nearer 3." — 8 % against 3 % is well under half, so 'much less fibre in the bottom than in the top' is exact.
A: "the wax he brought up from the bottom was in better condition than the wax at the top" — the deep wax is in better shape, not worn off.
B: "the grains he sieved came out much as the original specification had them" — the sand had hardly changed against spec.

C: "Eighty millimetres of it had not been turned since the day it was laid, and under nine years of hoofprints it had gone firm enough to lean a spade on." — below the tines the bed is the hard pan, the opposite of 'stayed loose'.
justification: The depth arithmetic reconciles: tines at 50 mm in a 130 mm bed leaves 130 - 50 = 80 mm unturned, exactly the figure given, and the fibre gradient (8 % top / ~3 % below) is the stated mechanism for the loose-over-hard layering. D is the only sampling finding not inverted by an explicit span.

findings: B (key): "In the schools laid on plain sand and fibre and kept damp with a sprinkler, the morning grid and the afternoon grid sit almost on top of one another." — plain sand and fibre = no wax, and the very next sentences supply the causal warrant: 'The waxed ones move, whatever their age' and 'The wax is a paraffin blend, and it is doing most of that work.'

A: "The waxed ones move, whatever their age." — age is explicitly ruled out, and 'He has the same pair of grids from a hundred and forty other arenas, some of them older than this one' shows the comparison set is not younger.
C: "laid over a membrane and crushed stone" — the membrane belongs to this waxed school's build-up and is never offered as a water-retaining feature of the sprinkler schools.
D: "He has the same pair of grids from a hundred and forty other arenas" — the same pair of grids means the same two hours, so a different reading hour cannot be hiding the change.
justification: The contrast in the passage is wax versus no wax with age explicitly neutralised, so B is the suggestion the text licenses. A and D are each killed by a single span; C invents a mechanism from a detail belonging to the school under test.

findings: A (key): "Here Pallenmoor is careful, and the care is the most useful thing about him." — and the closing valuation 'That is a good deal less than the trade’s brochures offer, and it is worth more than they are' makes his self-imposed limits the contribution.

B: "The yard has changed one thing and left the other alone." — the tine change is reported as an action taken, not as an answer to soundness, which the text puts out of reach: 'The tester measures a surface; there is no horse above the cone.'

C: "For two winters the riders here have been saying that the school changes under them" — the readings confirm the riders ('Both figures moved, and they moved together'); what they correct is the yard's blame - 'The yard has blamed the machine, then the mix, then the man on the tractor.'
D: "That is a good deal less than the trade’s brochures offer, and it is worth more than they are." — the brochures offer more and are worth less; D inverts the sentence.
justification: The writer's evaluative sentences are explicit and all point one way: the care is the most useful thing about him, and his restricted claim is worth more than the brochures' fuller one. C is the sharpest trap - the readings were brought in over a rider complaint - but the complaint is vindicated rather than corrected, and the correction lands on the yard's successive blaming.

findings: C (key): "The temperature is doing more in that room than the tractor is," — 'more than' concedes the tractor also matters, and the tine story supplies the second term: 'The leveller’s tines were set to 50 millimetres. The bed is 130.' with 'the machine had been slowly sorting the bed into a loose layer riding on a hard one'.

A: "Below about six degrees the coating is stiff, the grains lock together, and a hoof breaks the surface." — the locking mechanism is stiff paraffin, not ice; the cold readings are three and four degrees, i.e. above freezing ('with the school at three degrees', 'the thermometer beside them reads four').

B: "Above about twenty-five it goes slack, the grains slide past one another, and the floor gets deep." — a heated school need not reach the slack range, so it would ride like neither extreme; the text also refuses the quantitative bridge B needs - 'I can’t put a number on it; these readings won’t carry one'.
D: "The temperature is doing more in that room than the tractor is," — D inverts the ranking stated in the quotation.
justification: C is the synthesis the passage actually supports: temperature is the larger term and tine depth the smaller but real one, both shown to change how the floor rides. The temperature figures reconcile with the mechanism - 3 and 4 degrees sit below the ~6 degree stiffening point and the July afternoon sits above it - which is what kills A (no freezing is available at 3-4 degrees above zero) and blocks B (nothing puts a heated February school in the >25 slack range where July sits).

findings: C (key): "___(1)___, the ending is unanimous: five seconds later the sound stops, and again there has been no signal." — 'Equally' marks a parallel second instance of the same phenomenon, which is exactly what 'and again there has been no signal' signposts.

A: "No one has agreed to anything, there is no conductor to watch, and yet two hundred people find the same half-second." — 'Hence' asserts a consequence, but the unanimous ending does not follow from the unanimous start - they are two parallel instances.
B: "the ending is unanimous" — 'Rather' corrects or replaces a preceding claim; nothing here is being corrected, since both clauses assert unanimity.
D: "five seconds later the sound stops" — 'Elsewhere' shifts place, but the shift here is in time within the same hall.
justification: Pure connective item and the discourse relation is unambiguous: parallel addition, flagged by 'again'. Only 'Equally' encodes that relation; 'Hence' encodes consequence, 'Rather' correction, 'Elsewhere' a change of location, and each is blocked by the sentence it would have to join.

findings: A (key): "The risk of putting your hands together in a quiet room is that the room may not ___(2)___ in, and for the length of one clap you are alone with an opinion nobody asked for." — 'join in' is the fixed phrasal verb for others taking up an activity already started, and it is what the next sentence turns on: 'That is why the second pair of hands matters more than the first'.
B: "the room may not ___(2)___ in" — 'cut in' means to interrupt speech or movement; the room is not interrupting the clapper.
C: "the room may not ___(2)___ in" — bare 'fall in' is getting into formation; the agreement sense requires 'fall in with' plus an object.
D: "the room may not ___(2)___ in" — 'break in' is also interruption, and carries an intrusive sense at odds with joining the applause.
justification: Collocation item with one idiomatic fit. The three rejects are all interrupt-or-formation verbs, none of which can mean taking up an applause someone else has started, and none of which is licensed by the bare particle 'in' in this frame.

findings: B (key): "the coming-down is a ___(3)___ about how long is decent, conducted at speed and without words" — 'negotiation' is a process noun, takes 'about', and is what one 'conducts' - all three cues in the same clause.
A: "conducted at speed and without words" — a transaction is an exchange, is not 'about' a question of degree, and is not conducted in this sense.
C: "a ___(3)___ about how long is decent" — a bargain is the agreement reached, not the process being conducted, and the clause describes the sound still coming down.
D: "a ___(3)___ about how long is decent" — a settlement is likewise an outcome, and takes 'of' rather than 'about'; the sentence needs the ongoing haggling, not its result.
justification: The frame supplies three converging constraints - process noun, complement 'about', collocation with 'conducted' - and only 'negotiation' satisfies all three. The other three are outcome nouns, so they also clash with the aspect of 'the coming-down', which names something still in progress.

findings: D (key): "Although what a hall gives an eight-year-old is ___(4)___, it is not permitted to run long." — 'Although' demands a concession that pulls against brevity; 'wholehearted' does exactly that and is then quantified by 'Four or five seconds, then a ragged tail'.

A: "No one has agreed to anything, there is no conductor to watch" — 'rehearsed' contradicts the essay's premise that nothing about the applause is arranged, and gives the concessive clause nothing to concede.

B: "Although what a hall gives an eight-year-old is ___(4)___, it is not permitted to run long." — 'outspoken' describes frankness in speech, not applause, and carries no concessive pull against length.
C: "it is not permitted to run long" — 'brief' makes the concession self-defeating - 'although it is brief, it may not run long' restates the main clause instead of opposing it.
justification: Concessive-connector item. The gap must hold a quality that would otherwise license a long ovation; only 'wholehearted' does. C is the designed trap and is killed by the concession logic, since it would make the two halves of the sentence agree rather than contrast.

findings: B (key): "A room asked for a big hand for a stranger will give one ___(5)___, and everybody present can hear that it is not the same sound the recorder player got." — 'dutifully' names compliance without warmth, which is precisely the audible difference the clause reports.
A: "will give one ___(5)___" — 'narrowly' means barely or by a small margin and has no reading in which a room gives applause narrowly.
C: "A room asked for a big hand for a stranger" — 'instinctively' contradicts 'asked for' - the applause is prompted, not spontaneous - and would make it the genuine article.
D: "everybody present can hear that it is not the same sound the recorder player got" — 'eagerly' would make the prompted applause at least as warm as the real thing, which the clause denies.
justification: The second half of the sentence fixes the value: the sound is audibly lesser. Only 'dutifully' produces that; 'instinctively' and 'eagerly' both raise it, and 'narrowly' has no available sense here.

findings: A (key): "“It’s the stop at the far end that does it,” she says." — her own words, set against 'Between stations the shocks were tiny', locate the damage at arrival.
B: "Nothing shows on the ward; the colour comes with the spinning." — the pink plasma is only visible after centrifuging, so nothing can be spotted before the sample leaves the ward.
C: "Blood gases have never gone by tube; a porter walks those down." — blood gases are the one thing that does not go by tube.
D: "The loop runs at the speed it always has." — the speed is unchanged; the halved reject rate follows from 'Two bins are lined with foam'.
justification: A is a direct quotation and the contrast sentence before it rules out the in-transit alternative. B, C and D are each flatly inverted by one clause, and the closing line 'Nobody has lined the other bins' is consistent with the foam - not speed - being the change that halved rejects.

findings: D (key): "claimed the bank, the ditch and the timber from the stone gap down to the lane" — the pegged line runs 'from the ash to the culvert', and the passage plants the two landmarks in the claimed stretch: 'An ash grew in the stone gap; a culvert ran under the lane.' - same ground, which is the implication the item asks for.
A: "The neighbour’s attorney enclosed a tracing of the railway company’s deposited plan." — the plan is brought into the letters by the neighbour's own attorney.

B: "cut from above by one and cleaned from below by the other" — the hedge was maintained by both farms and 'both sides agree the thorn was last laid in 1839', six years before the claim and within a normal laying cycle; neglect is never suggested.

C: "The previous October a surveyor had chained and pegged the line along the bank, from the ash to the culvert." — the surveyor's October precedes the claim of 'In November 1845' and the letters that run from it to March, so he came before the attorneys wrote, not after.
justification: The chronology reconciles and is the point of the item: pegging in October 1845, claim in November 1845, letters to March 1846, offer in February to leave the timber and keep the ground, scheme abandoned autumn 1846, joint laying 1851. Matching the claim's bounds (stone gap to lane) to the pegged line's bounds (ash to culvert) via the two landmark sentences gives D, and the same date arithmetic kills C under any reading of 'the previous October', since both the November claim and the March close of the letters fall after it.

findings: C knyter dessutom takten till något hon inte går i god för: -> Dessutom binder C takten till ensemblen: (q1 rationale, C limb; NEW at fleet-repair-3, which added this sentence to close vote 2's correspondence gap. Two faults in one string. (a) The round avoided the lemma ”lova” in the run-up and kept its sense: ”går i god för” stands 10 tokens before the quotation's own ”kan jag inte lova”, so the reader is told the answer and then given it. Dropping the lexical echo without dropping the semantic one hides the stutter instead of removing it. (b) C is now the only distractor limb in either question with two sentences, and both open on ”C”, so the second reads as a new limb starting. The replacement opens elsewhere and names the ensemble without previewing the quotation's verb.

Symbolen är slingans, inte radens. Det är symbolen som återkommer på uppslagen, medan raden har en enda plats i höstprogrammet. -> Symbolen är slingans, inte radens. Raden själv har en enda plats i höstprogrammet. (q2 rationale, A/B limb; the second sentence is NEW at fleet-repair-3, which replaced an ambiguous ”den” with ”symbolen”. The anaphora repair was right — ”den” did stand immediately after ”radens” — but the round traded it for ”Symbolen”/”symbolen” 7 tokens apart across a sentence boundary, in a sentence whose first half restates the sentence before it. Cutting the restated half removes both the repetition and the redundancy and leaves the contrast the limb exists to draw.

Rätt svar A: skribenten kräver att textningen ska vara regel och inte undantag: ”Från -> Rätt svar A: skribenten kräver att textningen ska vara regel och inte undantag. ”Från (q1 rationale, key limb; NEW at fleet-repair-3, which converted the file's last full-stop-before-a-quotation into a colon so that the unit would carry ”one system rather than two”. The uniformity costs two things. The sentence now carries two colons, which is the fault this gate files in the passage of las-b22-001. And with the change made, all six sentences of the q1 rationale end colon-plus-quotation without exception; read aloud end to end the limb sequence becomes a metronome. The full stop the file carried for three rounds broke the beat once and cost nothing.
justification: Vote 1, read aloud as a native, two sentences either side of every changed span, then the two rationales end to end. fleet-repair-3 discharged the three pre-existing paraphrase-then-quote stutters this vote filed at r3 and discharged them well. ”vara regel och inte undantag” abstracts where the quotation specifies, which is the right shape, and it is a better string than the ”text på hela repertoaren” this vote prescribed — the round is correct that the repertoire includes lilla scenen, which the writer expressly leaves outside her demand, so my own string would have half-vouched for distractor D. ”det pris som ensemblen betalar” drops the kostnad lemma and says who bears it. ”en successiv utbyggnad” lands. The -vändning rhyme this vote filed as repair-introduced is gone, and the round was right to refuse my replacement, which would have put ”ett svepskäl” nine words in front of the quotation's own ”Ett svepskäl är det inte”. Three of five findings applied, one applied by a better route, one out of scope. What the round then wrote is three smaller things, all of them in the seams: a semantic pre-echo where a lexical one was removed, a repetition where an ambiguity was removed, and a metronome where a system was unified. Flag: three editor's fixes, none of them errors a student would call wrong.

findings: De andra kvällarna gissar jag mig fram genom andra akten -> De kvällar som saknar text gissar jag mig fram genom andra akten (passage §1; ORIGINAL GENERATOR COPY, carried through three rounds. Both r3 votes filed it, and both filed only half of it: ”andra” twice in seven words in two senses. The larger fault is reference. The two preceding sentences establish ”Raden rymmer fyra kvällar” and ”Jag har varit på tre av dem”, so the nearest available antecedent for ”De andra kvällarna” is the one remaining textad evening of the four — singular, and the wrong set. The sentence means the evenings without text, which are a different class entirely. The prescribed ”De övriga kvällarna” repairs the homonym and leaves the false antecedent standing.

Rätt svar D: texten säger vilka två kategorier raden ligger mellan: ”I länsteaterns höstprogram -> Rätt svar D: texten säger vilka två kategorier raden ligger mellan. ”I länsteaterns höstprogram (q2 rationale, key limb; written at fleet-repair-2 and untouched since. Two colons in one sentence. fleet-repair-3 did not repair it — it copied the shape into q1's key limb instead, on the ground that a colon before every quotation is one system. The unit now carries the fault twice where it carried it once.
justification: Vote 2, systematic grammar sweep on the final bytes. Both r3 items landed as written or better. The anaphoric ”den” after ”radens” is now ”symbolen”, which is the disambiguating repetition the repeated-noun rule carves out. The correspondence gap in the C limb is closed with the span this vote named, verified byte-identical, and ”vilket” is now ”som” with a nominal antecedent. Clean on: en/ett (en rad, ett svepskäl, en skärm, ett uppslag, en mottagare, en replik, ett spelår, ett annat motstånd); predicative agreement (inklämd on en rad, ”är den mörk” on skärmen, ”Ett svepskäl är det inte” with the correct neuter predicational det); pronoun gender on every anaphor, including the new B limb's ”den”, where the only common-gender candidate in reach is invändningen and motstånd is neuter; BIFF at every negation; subordinate word order; prepositions; compounds established, none coined; no non-words; no omitted som. D: faller på "och något förslag för den scenen har jag inte" — hon lämnar uttryckligen lilla scenen utan förslag.
justification: Stycket Ändå ska den bäras binder ihop de två halvorna av A: hon erkänner att spelet binds hårdare vid manus och kräver ändå textning på varje föreställning på stora scenen. De tre övriga motsägs var för sig av en explicit mening.

findings: A: faller på "Slingans symbol finns längst ned på varje uppslag i programbladet och har gjort det i alla år." — symbolen hör till uppslaget, inte till raden.
B: faller på samma mening — det som upprepas längst ned på varje uppslag är slingans symbol, inte raden.
C: faller på "Längre bak i programbladet står Ingegerd Hörnfeldt under rubriken Text och teknik." — namnet står längre bak, inte på raden.
D: bekräftas av "inklämd mellan syntolkning och skolföreställningar".
justification: Frågan gäller enbart raden i höstprogrammet. Två distraktorer flyttar över egenskaper från slingsymbolen och en från personsidan längre bak; bara D beskriver raden.

findings.span: Skaren som bar en karl gick sönder under hoven
findings.note: Direkt stöd: skaren som bar en gående karl brast under hoven, dvs. hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick. Förstärks av ett djur som trampade igenom skar upp benen på iskanten.

findings.span: mot det hjälper varken broddar eller lättare lass
findings.note: Texten säger uttryckligen att broddar inte hjälper mot hovtrycket; B påstår motsatsen.

findings.span: Lassen gick på kälke i stället, och kälken drogs för hand.
findings.note: Kälken drogs för hand, inte av häst; C flyttar dragarbetet tillbaka till hästen.

Att hästen fick stå i stallet är oförenligt med att den användes till annat. Caveat: texten uttalar sig bara om att hästen hölls utanför skarkörningen och är tyst om eventuell annan sysselsättning under resten av de veckorna; dödandet vilar alltså på ett litet slutledningssteg plus total avsaknad av stöd, inte på en punktvis motsägelse.

justification: Stycket om hästen ger ett entydigt svar: skaren som bar en karl brast under hoven eftersom en hov samlar hela tyngden på en tallriksstor yta. A är den enda formulering som återger detta. B motsägs ordagrant (broddar hjälper inte), C motsägs av att kälken drogs för hand, och D är oförenlig med att hästen fick stå i stallet. Inget annat alternativ går att försvara på texten.

findings.span: Man såg på himlen och bestämde sig kvällen innan.
findings.note: Stöds av Veckorna kom när de kom. och Somliga år blev det fyra morgnar på hela vintern, och ett par vintrar uteblev skaren. Friktion: att besluta kvällen innan är i strikt mening ett beslut i förväg; nyckeln kräver läsningen att i förväg avser planering längre fram än kvällen före. Kontexten (vädret avgör, veckorna kom när de kom) gör den läsningen klart rimligast, men lexikal friktion finns.

findings.span: Var gård körde för sig, och sällan väntade någon in grannen.
findings.note: Varje gård körde för sig och väntade sällan in grannen; det utesluter både turtagning och delat slit.

findings.span: Skidor dög till att ta sig fram med, men inte till att dra med.
findings.note: Uttrycklig motsägelse: skidor dög inte till att dra med. Lassen gick på kälke i stället, och kälken drogs för hand.

findings.span: Ett lass som inte är hemma vid tio blir liggande till nästa natt.
findings.note: Körningen slutade med bärigheten (vid tio är det över), inte när sista lasset var hemma; ett lass som inte hann hem blev liggande.

justification: Frågan gäller hur arbetet lades upp. A, C och D motsägs var för sig av en explicit mening i texten (var gård för sig; skidor dög inte till att dra med; lass som inte är hemma vid tio blir liggande). Kvar står B, som stöds av att veckorna kom när de kom, att skaren somliga vintrar uteblev helt, och att man såg på himlen och bestämde sig först kvällen innan. B är därmed enda försvarbara alternativ. Sänkt konfidens enbart för den lexikala friktionen mellan i förväg och bestämde sig kvällen innan; ingen andra försvarbar nyckel uppstår ur den friktionen, så item är svarbart.

findings: FORM PROFILE (the point of this pass). Consequence connective: “so” in A and D, 2/4, balanced. Explicit negation: A (“has not had”) and B (“no wax”), 2/4, balanced. Hedges and modals: 0/4, balanced, and critically there is no lone hedged option. Coordinate vs subordinate: A and D are two-clause coordinate, B is a pseudo-cleft with a finite free relative, C is one clause with coordinated VPs.

THE FORM DEFECT THE PREVIOUS ROUND INTRODUCED IS CLOSED. The three highest-signal form variables - consequence connective, explicit negation, hedge - are each balanced 2+2 or 0+4, and no option is the unique value of any of them.

Residual weak isolates exist but name three different options and none converges: B alone carries a finite embedded clause and the strict universal “all day”; C alone has a grammatical subject that is not the schools (“A membrane under them”) and the longest internal run; A alone carries a hard number (“nine years”).

FORM AND CONTENT DIVERGE, which is the safe configuration: the weak form isolate is B while the content-favoured option is C, so no compound route exists. Contrast las-b22-003 q2, where they converge.

Residual content channel, PAIR_STRUCTURE 2+2: A and D both explain the observation away as an artefact of his comparison (“nine years of hooves”; “the change falls between his two grids”), while B and C both assert the bed does not change through the day. PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE then collapses the set - the stem asks what is suggested about the schools, not about his measurement schedule, so A and D read as off-stem and the residual is B and C at 0.50.

The tie-break from B to C is WORLD_KNOWLEDGE and expert-only: it is waxed footing, not unwaxed, that rides the same all day, so B inverts the physics. An HP candidate cannot run this step and stops at 0.50.
justification: Student floor about 0.50 by a student-available stem-relevance route (2x base); expert floor about 0.75. 0.50 is a real lift but short of the roughly 0.60 kill bar, so flag. The form channel this repair targeted is genuinely closed; what survives is a content pairing, and the surviving pair is the one the stem points at.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE, expert-only: haemolysis in pneumatic-tube transport is a deceleration artefact, which favours A, and haemolysis is not visible in whole blood before centrifugation, which marks B false. Neither step is available to an HP candidate.
justification: Stems-only accuracy for a student about 0.27. My pick rests entirely on clinical domain knowledge the target population does not have, so it is not a channel.

findings: 3+1 exclusivity cluster (INERT, not scored): A, C and D all involve the railway survey, B attributes the quarrel to an untended thorn.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE, student-available: the stem asks what is implied. B states a cause outright (“The quarrel began because”) and C states bare chronology, so neither reads as an implication; the residual A and D sit at 0.50.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE / narrative schema, student-available: in a boundary quarrel that coincides with a railway survey, the hidden-motive reading - that the disputed ground is the pegged-out ground - is the one a strong reader reaches with no text in front of them. That is D.
Form balanced: word counts 14/13/13/14; no hedge or modal anywhere; the only negation-flavoured element is A’s “without bringing”, a 3+1 and inert.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.47 by a route a strong student can run unaided: eliminate the two non-inferential options, then take the motive reading. A real lift, below the roughly 0.60 kill bar, so flag rather than kill.

findings: 3+1 exclusivity cluster (INERT, not scored): A, C and D are recommendations built on ”bör” that differ only in extent, while B characterises the ensemble’s objection instead.
Form balanced: concessive subordinate clauses in A (”även om”) and D (”trots att”), other subordinate types in B and C; word counts 13/12/14/15; no hedge isolate and no explicit negation anywhere.

Test-wise pulls cancel: the strongest-opinion heuristic points at B, while the answers-the-stem heuristic points away from B because it is about the ensemble rather than about textning. Net lift zero.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.30 against a 0.25 base. The one content cluster is the inert 3+1 shape and the residual heuristics cancel.

findings: No stems-only route: the four options are independent facts about a listing line, none entailed or excluded by another.

Weak single-variable isolates name different options and do not converge: C alone embeds a finite clause (”vem som sköter tekniken”), B alone carries a universal quantifier (”varje uppslag”). Word counts 6/7/6/6; no hedge, modal or negation anywhere.
No CROSS_QUESTION support: nothing in q1’s option set bears on where a line sits in a programme.
justification: Stems-only accuracy about 0.27. My pick is a weak genre hunch about what a critical writer would single out, not a channel.

findings: RULE 15 leg (a), one-way leak: NOT PRESENT, in either direction. q2’s option set supplies only a programme line, a loop symbol, audio description and school performances, none of which bears on the writer’s stance in q1. q1’s option set supplies stage sizes, a caption strip and ensemble resistance, none of which supplies the listing q2 presupposes. No proposition needed by one question survives three of four options in the other.

RULE 15 leg (b), symmetric vouching: NOT PRESENT. The two sets share only the accessibility-services topic, which is a frame, not a variable. No option in either question constrains the truth of an option in the other.
The propositions that do survive 4/4 in each set - that the theatre captions some performances, that a printed listing exists - are supplied by the stems themselves, so they are not leaks.

JOINT STEMS-ONLY FLOOR: 0.30 x 0.27 = 0.081, i.e. 1.3x the 6.25 percent base. The two questions are also uncorrelated - getting one right tells a student nothing about the other - so the independent product is the honest figure here.
justification: Both legs of RULE 15 are clean and the joint floor sits at base within estimation error. This is what a passing Swedish pair looks like, and it is the direct contrast to las-b22-003.

findings: FORM_ISOLATE_D (convergent, soft): D is the only passive clause in the set (”användes”) and the only option built on a vague indefinite pro-form (”annat”). Its longest concrete run is 1 token against 6 / 5 / 3 for A / B / C. Two variables converge on one option, which is a channel by the calibration, but both are surface manifestations of a single latent trait (abstractness), so the channel is scored as roughly one and a half variables rather than two.

CANCELLED_ISOLATE_A: A is the only two-clause option (”Hovarna sjönk igenom där folk gick.”), isolated on clause structure alone. A single-variable isolate pointing at a different option than the D convergence, so it cancels and is not a channel.

INERT_SUBJECT_SPLIT: the set divides 2+2 on subject lexeme, ”Hovarna” in A and B against ”Hästarna” in C and D, with a 1-vs-1 contradiction inside each half (hooves broke through vs hooves coped; horses hauled vs horses were elsewhere). Two competing contradictory pairs cancel, so the contradictory-pair heuristic is inert here rather than a channel.

PARTIAL_STEM_FIT (weak): the stem ”Vad sägs i texten om hästarna?” names hästarna, which matches the grammatical subject of C and D only. Narrowing to those two is available passage-blind but unreliable, since hooves are transparently part of horses. Worth a few points, not an elimination.
INERT_AXES: explicit negation, absolutizers and hedges or modals are absent from all four options. Three uniform axes, therefore inert, and no lone hedged option exists.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE non-decisive: ”broddar” (ice studs) on working horses is historically standard, so B is factually plausible without the passage, but A is equally plausible physically. No option is knocked in or out on facts alone.
justification: Base 25 percent. The only directional route a passage-blind student has is the convergent form isolation on D: three vivid, concrete, lexically specific options against one abstract agentless restatement. In LÄS the abstract restatement is more often the key than chance, because distractors are usually assembled from the passage surface vocabulary, so a form-reading student lands on D above chance. The lift is real but capped, because the two converging variables are one underlying trait and because the folklore direction (odd option as key vs odd option as throwaway) is not settled. The weak stem-subject match adds a little more mass to the {C, D} half. Estimated blind accuracy roughly 38 percent against a 25 percent base: a real lift, far below the kill line. Verdict flag.

findings: TWO_COMPETING_CONVERGENCES (net: no exploitable isolate): C is convergently isolated as the only s-passive (”släpades”) and the only option that is concrete end to end, a run of 7 of 7 tokens. B is convergently isolated as the only expletive agentless subject (”Det”), the only impossibility modal (”gick inte att”) and the only propositional negation. Two options convergently isolated in opposite directions cancel each other as an attention channel.

INERT_NEGATION_AXIS: explicit negation surfaces in B (”inte”) and in D (”Inte förrän”), a 2+2 split on the strict surface reading and therefore not an isolate. B stands alone only under the narrower propositional-negation reading, which is why its convergence is scored soft.

ABSOLUTIZER_ISOLATE_D: D alone carries absolutizing framing (”sista lasset” plus ”tog körningen slut” under a not-until frame) and alone fronts a subordinate clause with V2 inversion. A third marked option, which disperses the odd-one-out signal further rather than concentrating it.

STEM_FIT_ROUTE (the real blind lift): the stem ”Vad framgår av texten om hur arbetet lades upp?” asks about organisation. C (”Lassen släpades fram på skidor över myren.”) answers a conveyance question instead, and D answers a duration or endpoint question. That leaves A as the only positive organisational claim and B as the negative one. A student who applies stem fit narrows to {A, B} and then prefers the positive claim, reaching A without the passage.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE_PULL_A: rotation between households is the canonical historical arrangement for Swedish rural winter hauling, so ”Hushållen turades om och delade på slitet.” is generically plausible on background knowledge alone. This reinforces the stem-fit route rather than forming a second independent one, so the two are not multiplied.

NO_MIRRORED_TWIN: no two options are near-paraphrases. The four claims sit on four different variables: division of labour, schedulability, conveyance, endpoint. There is no 3+1 exclusivity cluster either, so nothing inert to discount.
justification: Base 25 percent. Form gives a blind student nothing usable: three of four options are marked, and the two genuinely convergent isolates (B and C) point in opposite directions and cancel. The lift comes from semantics, not form. The stem asks how the work was laid out, and only two of the four options answer that question at all, so stem fit alone removes C as a conveyance claim and discounts D as an endpoint claim. Between the survivors, A is the positive organisational answer and is independently plausible on background knowledge about communal rotation. The chain is three defensible but unforced steps, so the population figure sits near the low end of what a careful student achieves: roughly 42 percent against a 25 percent base. Real lift, below the kill line. Verdict flag. The underlying weakness is that the key is partly recoverable from stem fit alone.

findings: LEG_A, direction q2 to q1: CLOSED. No proposition in the Q2 option set reaches the strong form of 3 of 4 on anything Q1 needs. On the horse-use variable Q2 splits 1 assert-for (”körningen” in D implies horse-driving in this register), 1 assert-against (”skidor” in C implies human traction), and 2 silent (A on division of labour, B on schedulability). A 1-1-2 split whose two carriers contradict each other is noise, not a leak.

LEG_A, direction q1 to q2: OPEN but weak and new. Q1 supplies the proposition that the work took place on winter snow and ice, at 3 of 4. B asserts it (”broddar” are ice studs), C asserts it (”kälken” is a sledge), A presupposes it (”sjönk igenom” requires ice or crust to break through); D is silent. Neither stem supplies the season, and the proposition survives whichever option is the key, because a distractor can be false about the horses while still presupposing the same winter world.

LEAK_YIELD_LOW: the winter proposition lifts Q2-B (variable ice conditions make fixing days ahead implausible) and Q2-C (skis require snow) in the same direction and by similar amounts. It widens the Q2 field instead of narrowing it, so it is a real one-way leak with poor conversion, and it is not the dominant blind route in either question.

LEG_B, symmetric vouching: DIFFUSE, not a channel. Three mutually incompatible alliances exist. Q1-C with Q2-D is the horse-drawn hauling world. Q1-D with Q2-C is the no-horse world. Q1-A or Q1-B with Q2-B is the unreliable-footing-means-unschedulable-days world. Vouching is a channel only when one alliance stands out; three competing alliances raise the confidence of whichever pair a student already favours without indicating which to favour.

CONSISTENCY_MATRIX_DENSE: of the 16 key combinations only 2 are even softly excluded, (Q1-C, Q2-C) and (Q1-D, Q2-D), and both survive a charitable narrative reading, since a text can describe sledge haulage on the road and ski haulage over the mire, and ”körningen” does not strictly require a horse. Cross-question consistency filtering is therefore close to inert, which is the clearest evidence that the old pair-level kill condition is gone.
FLOOR_INDEPENDENT: 0.38 times 0.42 equals 0.16, that is 2.6 times the 6.25 percent base.
FLOOR_CORRELATED: were the pair decided by one proposition, the joint would collapse to about one coin at 0.42 to 0.50. Rejected as the honest reading.

HONEST_READING is the independent product, roughly 16 percent. The two blind routes differ in kind, Q1 by form isolation on abstractness and Q2 by semantic stem fit, and share no deciding proposition; solving one gives no purchase on the other. The correlated reading would only be honest if a single world-proposition selected both keys, and the near-complete consistency matrix shows it does not.
justification: The RULE 15 condition that killed this pair is not present in the repaired sheet. Leg (a) from Q2 into Q1 is closed: the Q2 option set no longer carries any proposition at 3-of-4 strength that Q1 needs, and its only two horse-relevant options assert opposite things while the other two abstain. Leg (b) is defused by multiplicity rather than by absence: three vouching alliances exist and they partition the grid incompatibly, so the structure cannot select a key. The consistency matrix is dense, excluding 2 of 16 cells and both only softly. What has appeared is a weaker leak running the other way, Q1 into Q2, supplying the winter setting at 3 of 4 from neither stem and surviving any key assignment. It qualifies as a strong-form one-way leak but converts badly, because it lifts two Q2 options together without discriminating between them. Joint stems-only floor is 16 percent against a 6.25 percent base on the honest independent reading, which is a genuine lift and well short of the roughly 60 percent kill line. Verdict flag at pair level, driven by the per-question weaknesses rather than by the residual leak.

findings: A (cone driven to the bottom of the bed at every point) dies on: "how many blows take it to a hundred millimetres"; "The floor is 130 millimetres of washed silica sand"
B (weight dropped by hand from a height chosen per point) dies on: "a steel cone on a rod, under a ring weight raised to a collar and let fall"

justification: Key C is stated outright: two-thirds as deep is a shallower first blow and a nearly doubled count is a higher count. A dies on the instrument's stated stopping depth (100 mm) against the stated bed depth (130 mm); B dies on the fixed drop height (raised to a collar); D is the exact reversal of Pallenmoor's quoted comparison. Every non-key option is contradicted by a stated fact, none is merely unmentioned. Key C support: "in the cold the first blow took the cone two-thirds as deep, and the count nearly doubled"

findings: A (wax worn off the grains lower down) dies on: "the wax he brought up from the bottom was in better condition than the wax at the top"
B (sand broken down finer than specification) dies on: "the grains he sieved came out much as the original specification had them"

C (bed below the tines stayed loose, out of reach of hoofprints) dies on: "Eighty millimetres of it had not been turned since the day it was laid, and under nine years of hoofprints it had gone firm enough to lean a spade on."
justification: Key D is the cored-sample result in figures (about 8 per cent top, nearer 3 lower down). A, B and C are each the direct negation of a stated finding: bottom wax in better condition, grains as specified, and the unturned 80 mm gone firm under hoofprints. No second option survives. Key D support: "In the top 50 millimetres the fibre came out at about 8 per cent by weight; lower down it was nearer 3."

findings: A (sprinkler schools are newer, sand has had less wear) dies on: "He has the same pair of grids from a hundred and forty other arenas, some of them older than this one."; "The waxed ones move, whatever their age."

C (a membrane under them holds water in and stops the bed drying) dies on: "laid over a membrane and crushed stone"; "Both figures moved, and they moved together"; "The waxed ones move, whatever their age."; "kept damp with a sprinkler"; "The wax is a paraffin blend, and it is doing most of that work."

D (they are read at other hours so the change falls between the grids) dies on: "He has the same pair of grids from a hundred and forty other arenas"; "the morning grid and the afternoon grid sit almost on top of one another"
justification: REWRITTEN OPTION C VERIFIED REFUTED, NOT MERELY UNMENTIONED. The passage's only membrane is under the school being tested - 'laid over a membrane and crushed stone' - and that school is on the moving side of the contrast ('Both figures moved, and they moved together'; 'The waxed ones move, whatever their age').
